RoboSystems 1.13.0 is the release where the AI runs on the model you choose.
The operators moved onto Bedrock's Converse API behind a model registry, and a
stack you run yourself can now point them at an open-weight model on any
OpenAI-compatible server. That makes the open-source distribution open source
end to end: the code, the engines it runs on, and the AI. The release closes
the 1.12 series (48 pull requests since v1.12.0) with stronger guarantees
around closed months, the published documentation catalog, and a run of
search, serialization and fleet fixes. A Plaid bank feed is built into the
series and stays off in hosted production for now.

## The AI runs on the model you choose

- **One request shape for every model** (#1405, 1.12.5). The operator client
  moved from `InvokeModel` with an Anthropic-shaped body to Bedrock
  **Converse**, so Claude, GPT-5.6 and the open-weight families all run
  through a single tool protocol. The hard-coded Claude enum became a
  **model registry** keyed by profile (`economy` / `balanced` / `quality`), so
  which model an operator uses is a registry row, not a code path. The token
  meter resolves its rate through the same registry and **raises on an
  unregistered model** instead of billing it at a default rate. Hosted
  operators stay on Claude Sonnet 5; nothing customer-facing changed.
- **A self-hosted model provider, off by default** (#1436). Set
  `OPENAI_COMPAT_ENABLED` and the operators can run on any server that speaks
  the OpenAI Chat Completions API with tool calling — vLLM, Ollama, LM Studio,
  or a hosted API catalog. `OPERATOR_PROFILE_ECONOMY` / `_BALANCED` /
  `_QUALITY` map each tier to it; a tier left unmapped stays on Bedrock, and
  with all three mapped the stack needs no AWS credentials for AI. Converse
  stays the canonical transcript and the provider translates at the edge, so
  the tool loop and the operators are unchanged. When the flag is off the
  model does not exist in the registry, so nothing can resolve to it. Calls
  bill at rates you set, defaulting to zero. MCP clients always brought their
  own model; this closes the other lane.
- **Tested on open weights.** Against a demo ledger with twelve questions whose
  answers were computed independently, Kimi K3 and GLM 5.3 Flash answered all
  twelve correctly through the new provider, as Claude Sonnet 5 did, and GLM
  5.3 answered every question it completed. A model small enough for one
  workstation GPU did not. Setup and the tested models are on the
  [Local Development](https://robosystems.ai/docs/technical/local-development)
  page.
- **Ledger amounts are stated in dollars** (#1438). The graph holds dollars
  while the close and schedule tools speak integer cents, and one tool's
  description told every model that line amounts were cents. Smaller models
  carried that into graph queries and reported figures a hundred times too
  small. The unit is now stated on `read-graph-cypher` and in
  `get-example-queries` for ledger graphs, and the cents note is scoped to its
  own tool. On the model that made the error, it went from 5 runs in 20 to 0.
  RoboInvestor positions get the same statement (#1440): the API returns
  `cost_basis` and `current_value` in cents, and the graph holds dollars under
  the same names.

## Ledger integrity

- **Reversals and auto-reversing schedules** (#1401, 1.12.3). Reversing a
  journal entry nets to zero, and an auto-reversing schedule keeps its
  reversing entry across later periods.
- **One closing entry per schedule period** (#1402, 1.12.3), enforced by the
  database rather than by convention, with the schedule row locked while it is
  written.
- **Closed months stay closed** (#1407, 1.12.5). Curation that would change
  what a closed month's statements mean is refused, not only curation that
  would remove its history, and `reopen-period` accepts only the latest closed
  period.
- **A shared report keeps its filing status** (#1424, 1.12.7). A filed report
  shared into another graph arrives filed, not as a draft.

## Reports and serialization

- A tenant concept's label reaches the holon, not only the XBRL export
  (#1391), and a disclosure's calculation arcs are bundled once, so tenant
  notes no longer foot to twice their total (#1395).
- A tenant report's holon no longer describes itself as an SEC filing (#1406).
- The committed demo artifacts are gated on content, not only on SHACL shape:
  labels, cross-form agreement, declared arc endpoints and duplicate arcs
  (#1394, #1398).

## MCP and documentation

- **`/v1/mcp/roboledger`** (#1416, 1.12.6): a graph-agnostic, OAuth-only MCP
  endpoint for RoboLedger graphs, so the accounting workflow can be listed as a
  plugin of its own.
- **The documentation is published and indexable** (#1421, #1422, #1425,
  #1430, #1431). The technical docs and the product guides publish to the
  content CDN and render at `robosystems.ai/docs` and `roboledger.ai/docs`,
  including seven new RoboLedger guides on planning, mapping, schedules and the
  app. The handshake instructions cite the public pages (#1426).
- **`/docs` retires** (#1427, 1.12.7) and answers `301` to the per-operation
  reference at `robosystems.ai/docs/api`; `/` keeps the Swagger console,
  marked `noindex`. Three operation summaries lost a parenthetical (#1428).
- The RoboLedger guides are written for any AI assistant rather than for
  Claude, and the MCP instructions record an assistant's bank-feed
  classification as `ai` rather than `claude` (#1441).

## Search and SEC

- **Foreign private issuers enter search** (#1403, 1.12.4): both text index
  assets now take the 20-F, covering the 3,011 20-F reports on the shared
  graph as they are indexed. xbrlkit 0.16.3 fixes sections that ran past
  their own end, addresses indexed as sections and real sections dropped as
  pointers (#1404).
- **Stable hybrid ranking** (#1423, 1.12.7): a document scores the same at every
  page size, paging a hybrid search works, and one filer's consecutive filings
  of a section can fold into a single hit.
- **fp16 vectors** (#1410, 1.12.5): the index mapping takes fp16 scalar
  quantization, which halves the vector memory, with the tooling to rebuild the
  index from source. Recreating it now proves the executing role can both
  delete and create before it deletes anything (#1412), and search orphans can
  be swept by when they were indexed (#1389).
- xbrlkit 0.17.1, with `information-block` taking the same `offset` paging as
  `xbrlkit serve` (#1414); the pin is capped to one minor (#1396).

## Plaid, built and off in hosted production

- **Plaid on a shared bank-feed lane** (#1415, 1.12.6). The source-agnostic
  parts of the Mercury feed, account linking and the sync bookkeeping, moved
  into `adapters/bank_feed/`, and the Plaid provider and pipeline are built on
  them. The same bank account connected through two feeds gets its own chart
  account rather than the feeds overwriting each other's link. Gated by
  `CONNECTION_PLAID_ENABLED`, which defaults to off and stays off in hosted
  production for now.
- **Hardened before it ships on** (#1417, #1418, #1419, #1420, 1.12.6). A
  post-merge review drove four follow-ups: a restated bank line posts what the
  bank now says, the first sync waits for Plaid's historical pull, a re-linked
  Item re-keys its history instead of capturing it twice, transfer legs settle
  against a posted counterpart, and disconnect scrubs the feed's payloads
  wherever they sit. The QuickBooks, Mercury and Plaid connect flows now take
  the same per-connection lock for their first sync.

## Platform, infrastructure and CI

- The graph capacity alarm watches the stream the allocator actually publishes,
  and free tenant slots are reported per tier (#1400).
- The writer-tier availability zone is a guarded deploy parameter, so a
  relocation survives later releases and a release cannot move the fleet by
  accident (#1409).
- The shared replica fleet's Spot pool is wider, below the on-demand price
  (#1433).
- A running SSM command is no longer reported as a failed one (#1408).
- Production container scans are filed under `main`, so code-scanning alerts
  describe what is deployed (#1434).
- Local development: Postgres, Valkey, OpenSearch and LocalStack run on named
  volumes, `just clean-volumes` wipes them, and the local Postgres settings are
  pinned (#1435, #1437).
- Dependencies: anyio 4.14.2, soupsieve 2.9 (#1429, #1432); the `uv` guard note
  is trimmed (#1399); xbrlkit 0.16.0 (#1392); the demo scripts' client floor is
  1.17.2 (#1442).

## Deploying this release

- **New to production**: ten pull requests (#1432–#1438, #1440–#1442). The rest
  of the series shipped in 1.12.1–1.12.8.
- **Migration**: one in the series, extensions `0036` (one closing entry per
  schedule period), shipped in 1.12.3 and already applied wherever that patch
  was deployed. A fresh environment applies it at boot.
- **Stack updates** ride the deploy: `graph-ladybug-replicas` takes the wider
  Spot pool. Earlier in the series, `bastion` gained the OpenSearch put and
  delete verbs, and `graph-infra` the corrected capacity alarm. Every parameter
  is supplied by the workflows.
- **Owner steps**: none.
- **Feature flags**: `OPENAI_COMPAT_ENABLED` defaults off and stays off in
  hosted production; `OPERATOR_PROFILE_*` are unset, so every tier keeps its
  Bedrock model. `CONNECTION_PLAID_ENABLED` defaults off and stays off in
  hosted production. New secrets: `PLAID_CLIENT_ID`, `PLAID_SECRET` and
  `PLAID_ENVIRONMENT` for a deployment that turns Plaid on, and
  `OPENAI_COMPAT_API_KEY` for one that turns the provider on.
- **Images**: this tag publishes the first Docker Hub image with the
  self-hosted provider.
- **SDKs**: `robosystems-client` and `@robosystems/client` moved from 1.17.0
  to 1.17.2 across the series, regenerated for Plaid, `disclosures`, grouped
  search results and the three summaries; 1.17.2 points the API reference link
  at the published pages. Nothing on the stable tier changes,
  and the model registry and the self-hosted provider add no API surface.
